CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the correct order for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Cut, trim, burn, cool
   B. Cool, burn, trim, cut
   C. Trim, cool, burn, cut
   D. Burn, cut, trim, cool

2. Which is a melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Claves
   B. Kayamba
   C. Xylophone
   D. Cowbell

3. If you tighten the skin of a drum, the sound becomes (1 mark)
   A. lower
   B. higher
   C. silent
   D. softer for ever

4. Which tool is good for smudging charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. A finger or a tissue
   B. A wet brush of paint
   C. A knife
   D. A stone

5. Which players are allowed to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. Only C
   B. GK and GD
   C. WA and WD
   D. GS and GA

6. Which attacker may NOT enter the goal circle? (1 mark)
   A. GA
   B. GS
   C. None
   D. WA

7. Macramé is a technique of (1 mark)
   A. tying knots to make patterns and shapes
   B. painting on cloth
   C. carving wood
   D. beating drums

8. What is the main reason for improvising a netball? (1 mark)
   A. To spend more money
   B. To use available materials when balls are not enough
   C. To avoid playing
   D. Because real balls are always bad

9. Which colours are the primary colours? (1 mark)
   A. Red, yellow and blue
   B. Orange, green and purple
   C. Black, white and grey
   D. Red, green and brown

10. How many boxes are on the scale strip in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Five
   C. Ten
   D. One

11. A flat brush is best for (1 mark)
   A. tiny details only
   B. writing with ink
   C. cutting paper
   D. wide areas

12. Which shows neatness in a montage? (1 mark)
   A. Torn edges
   B. Glue everywhere
   C. Loose pieces
   D. Clean cut edges and no glue marks

13. How many beats does each bar have in the four-beat patterns of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Six
   C. Four
   D. Two

14. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. Two quavers equal one crotchet
   B. One quaver equals two crotchets
   C. A crotchet is shorter than a quaver
   D. A rest is longer than a note

15. Which of these letters is a tall letter with an ascender? (1 mark)
   A. t
   B. u
   C. n
   D. x

16. The line on which letters sit is called the (1 mark)
   A. baseline
   B. descender line
   C. border
   D. ascender line

17. Which tune ends on the home note? (1 mark)
   A. d r m r
   B. d r m r d
   C. r m r m
   D. m r m r

18. The Kodaly hand sign for d is (1 mark)
   A. a sloping palm
   B. a flat hand held level
   C. a pointing finger
   D. a closed fist

19. Variation in a melody means using (1 mark)
   A. different syllables and note lengths
   B. no rhythm
   C. only rests
   D. only one syllable

20. The sol-fa syllable d is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. day
   B. dee
   C. dah
   D. doh

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. What does giving with the ball mean in netball catching? (2 marks)

22. Describe how you would improvise a rhythm to accompany a song. (4 marks)

23. State three ways of showing fair play in a netball game. (3 marks)

24. Describe how to critique a friend's rhythmic pattern with respect. (4 marks)

25. Name four guide lines used for free hand lettering. (4 marks)

26. How can you show that you have identified the pitch of a note by ear? (3 marks)

27. Describe how to play a mini-netball game safely and fairly from warm-up to the end. (5 marks)

28. Explain what overlapping is and why it is used in a montage. (3 marks)

29. Why should a short melody end on d? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Cut, trim, burn, cool
   The stages are cutting, trimming, burning, then cooling.

2. C — Xylophone
   A xylophone has bars that give different notes, so it can play a tune.

3. B — higher
   A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher sound.

4. A — A finger or a tissue
   A finger or tissue blends charcoal softly.

5. D — GS and GA
   Only the Goal Shooter and the Goal Attack may score.

6. D — WA
   The Wing Attack plays in the centre and goal thirds but not in the circle.

7. A — tying knots to make patterns and shapes
   Macramé is done by tying cords in knots.

8. B — To use available materials when balls are not enough
   Improvising lets us practise with materials we already have.

9. A — Red, yellow and blue
   Primary colours cannot be made by mixing other colours.

10. B — Five
   The strip is divided into five equal boxes.

11. D — wide areas
   Flat brushes cover wide areas quickly.

12. D — Clean cut edges and no glue marks
   Neatness means careful cutting and pasting.

13. C — Four
   The patterns of this lesson have four beats.

14. A — Two quavers equal one crotchet
   1/2 + 1/2 = 1 beat.

15. A — t
   The letter t is a tall letter, with a stem that rises above small letters.

16. A — baseline
   All letters sit on the baseline.

17. B — d r m r d
   Only d r m r d ends on d.

18. D — a closed fist
   Doh is shown with a fist.

19. A — different syllables and note lengths
   Variation makes a tune interesting.

20. D — doh
   The syllable d is doh.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Bending the arms as the ball arrives so as to take the force out of it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bending arms, 1 mark for softening the catch.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing the song and find the beat by tapping. Play the beat on an instrument. Change to a pattern, such as two quick sounds and a long sound. Repeat it and change it at the end of a verse.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step, up to 4.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Follow the rules; respect the umpire; shake hands with the other team; take turns in positions; encourage teammates. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Say one good thing first. Talk about the steadiness of the beat, variation and the ending. Give one suggestion to make it better. Listen to others' views politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the note, decide if it is low, middle or high, and make the hand sign for it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for deciding pitch, 1 mark for hand sign.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up with jogging and stretching. Choose fair teams and positions. Check the ground and the ball. Move into space, pass early and play your position. Follow the rules, obey the umpire and thank the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage: warm-up, fair teams, checking, playing skills, fair ending.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Overlapping means placing one piece so it partly covers another. It removes gaps and makes the montage look full and joined up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reasons.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: d is the home note. Ending on it makes the melody sound finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each idea.
